currentContext.strengths: Market leader in Indian EVs for 7 consecutive years with 40.2% market share and cumulative EV sales past 250,000 units|Second-largest OEM in the Indian domestic PV market in H2 FY26 with 14.2% market share, growing at nearly twice the industry rate|Balanced multi-powertrain strategy (ICE, CNG, EV) driving broad-based growth across SUVs, hatchbacks and CNG variants|JLR's House of Brands structure -- four distinctive British brands (Range Rover, Defender, Discovery, Jaguar), each with shared design/engineering/technology foundations|Doubled its sales and service network across India over the past few years, enhancing customer access and convenience
currentContext.strategies: Multi-powertrain strategy spanning ICE, CNG and EV to cater to diverse mobility needs and comprehensively cover customer segments and price points|Continued portfolio strengthening through new nameplates (e.g. Sierra) and mid-cycle refreshes (Altroz, Punch, Harrier, Safari) across hatchbacks, sedans and SUVs|Network expansion and digital/AI-enabled customer experience improvements across sales, service and the ownership journey|Cost optimisation through value engineering and commercial levers to mitigate commodity headwinds; de-bottlenecking production capacity across plants|Addressing EV adoption barriers -- affordability, range confidence, battery assurance -- via aggressive cost engineering, Battery-as-a-Service (BaaS) offerings and lifetime battery warranty|Building a comprehensive EV charging ecosystem through open collaboration with charging-ecosystem players, including a network of Tata.ev Mega Charging hubs|Driving greater localisation of EV components to strengthen supply-chain resilience, mitigate geopolitical risk, and qualify for the PLI scheme|JLR continuing its flexible powertrain strategy (ICE/MHEV/PHEV) ahead of its first all-electric Range Rover and Jaguar launches, while building its Modern Luxury / House of Brands franchise|The Board recommends dividends based on parameters laid down in the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy (adopted pursuant to SEBI Listing Regulations Reg. 43A), with dividends paid out of the year's profits. For FY26, the Board recommended a final dividend of ₹3 per fully paid-up equity share of face value ₹2 (150%), subject to shareholder approval at the AGM.
currentContext.expansion: Production capacity was expanded across facilities in FY26 through de-bottlenecking interventions at all plants, supporting a sharp increase in production during H2. The Company inaugurated the new Panapakkam plant in Tamil Nadu -- a shared manufacturing facility with JLR -- to support future capacity expansion. Pursuant to the Composite Scheme of Arrangement demerging the Commercial Vehicle business, the Chinchwad facility in Pune, Maharashtra became part of the Company (TMPVL) with effect from October 2025, adding a manufacturing site to the PV business. The Company also expanded its dealer network, adding more than 100 sales outlets and more than 100 service outlets during the year. R&D and capex investments toward product sustainability -- particularly zero-emission products and battery electric vehicle technologies -- are undertaken through TPEML (Tata Passenger Electric Mobility Limited), the Company's wholly owned subsidiary.

risks.risk: Large multi-year capex commitment funded primarily by internal accruals
risks.note: JLR is investing GBP 18bn over five years from FY24 across its industrial footprint, vehicle programmes, autonomous/AI/digital technologies and people; TMPVL announced plans to invest ~Rs 33,000-35,000 crore for the PV/EV business between FY26-FY30. Management states this spend will be well funded primarily through internal cash accruals, with debt/incentives as backup, but this is a material step-up in investment against global headwinds such as tariffs and geopolitical uncertainty.

A cyber incident during Q2 FY26 required JLR to pause production for five weeks, contributing directly to a swing from consolidated net cash of Rs 1,018 crore (March 2025) to consolidated net debt of Rs 30,710 crore (March 2026) and a free cash outflow of Rs 26,823 crore in FY26, demonstrating the balance-sheet impact of an operational disruption event.

risks.risk: Trade-policy / tariff exposure on JLR's export markets
risks.note: Incremental US tariffs affecting JLR exports from the UK and EU to the USA were a primary driver of the 8.3% decline in FY26 consolidated revenue and the sharp compression in Underlying EBITDA margin (13.4% to 6.8%) and Underlying EBIT margin (7.6% to 1.1%), showing significant earnings sensitivity to geopolitical trade actions.

risks.risk: Restrictions on cash upstreaming from JLR to the parent
risks.note: JLR's UKEF facilities and its GBP 1.66 billion revolving credit facility include 'restricted payment' covenants and a minimum-liquidity requirement; the amount of cash JLR can transfer to TMPVL and its subsidiaries as dividends, loans or investments is capped at 25% of JLR's Profit After Tax, structurally limiting the parent's access to JLR's cash generation.

risks.risk: Financial and negative covenants across financing agreements
risks.note: Financing and debt arrangements set limits on, or require lender consent for, undertaking new projects, issuing new securities, management changes, mergers, sales of undertakings and investments in subsidiaries, and include financial covenants (e.g. net-worth ratios); breach could raise costs or restrict funding flexibility, though the Company states it was compliant with all applicable covenants in FY25 and FY26.

risks.risk: Structural dependence on the JLR segment for consolidated scale
risks.note: Automotive operations are TMPVL's most significant segment, with JLR historically the larger contributor to consolidated revenue and profitability; the FY26 tariff and cyber-incident impacts on JLR flowed through disproportionately to consolidated results even as the standalone/PV business grew.

one-line thesis: TMPV delivered a record Q4 with 37% YoY volume growth driven by GST 2.0 and new launches, offsetting JLR's difficult year marked by cyber incidents and tariffs. The strategic pivot focuses on JLR's GBP 1.7bn cost-out to reset breakeven to 300k units while TMPV leverages supply constraints to drive industry-beating growth in FY27 despite commodity headwinds.
financial scorecard: Revenue: ~Rs 105,000 Cr (+7% YoY); EBITDA Margin: 9.4% (Q4), 4.7% EBIT (FY26 full year muted by H1 pricing); PAT: Rs 2,500 Cr (FY26 PBT pre-exceptionals), excludes Rs 4,100 Cr one-offs (cyber, labor code, demerger stamp duty); Order Book: Healthy across models, 20 days inventory (India), tight globally; Net Debt: Rs 30,000 Cr (Consol), JLR Rs 33,000 Cr, PV Cash Positive Rs 7,000 Cr.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Industry ~10% (H1 high double-digit); Margin: Focus on cost reduction to offset 5-6% commodity hit; Order Inflow: EV bookings up 25-30% post-crisis; Capex: Rs 4,300 Cr (7.5% of rev) for PV, GBP 3.57bn for JLR (64% engineering).
order book & pipeline: India dealer inventory at 20 days; Waiting periods 4-8 weeks (Sierra/EVs higher); JLR inventory tight, US stocks deliberately reduced pre-tariff; 78k expressions of interest for Range Rover EV.
segment / subsidiary detail: PV: 6.42 lakh units (+15% YoY), Q4 >2 lakh units; EV: 92k units (+43% YoY), 40% market share; CNG: 27% of portfolio; JLR: 308k wholesales (FY26), Defender/RR strong, Jaguar down 5.7k units in Q4 due to transition.
growth verticals / optionality: Sierra ramp-up (target >10k/month); Sierra.ev launch next quarter; Range Rover EV/Sport EV production start H2; Freelander brand licensing royalty via CJLR; EMA architecture launch.
margins & cost dynamics: Commodity headwind 5-6% of revenue (3.5-4% hit in Q4); Absorbed 2% via cost reduction; 0.5% price hike implemented in April; JLR VME at 7%; Targeting GBP 1.7bn savings over 2 years.
capex / expansion: PV: Rs 4,300 Cr (capacity ramp, new launches); JLR: GBP 3.57bn (GBP 2.6bn engineering for 3 new architectures, BEV powertrains in Wolverhampton).
capital allocation: Dividend Rs 3/share (Rs 1,100 Cr outflow); Total group dividend Rs 7/share including TMLCV; FCF Q4: Rs 11,000 Cr (consol), Rs 1,700 Cr (PV); Prioritizing deleveraging JLR and funding EV transition.
risks & watch-items: Middle East conflict impacting supply chain (freight, petrochemicals) and MENA demand (6% mix); Geopolitical tariffs (US); Commodity inflation (Aluminum/Copper); JLR warranty costs; Regulatory volatility (CAFE, Made in Europe).
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic on demand; Aggressive on cost mitigation; Transparent on JLR challenges; Disciplined on inventory management; Focused on execution of launches.
non-obvious takeaways: JLR's breakeven volume reset to 300k units is critical to offset structural tariff/FX costs; PV's EV profitability trajectory is deflationary vs inflationary ICE due to emission norms; Freelander resurrection generates royalty/toll revenue without capex burden on JLR.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Domestic demand continues to sustain, led by growth in SUVs, CNG and EV; geopolitical developments remain a key monitorable for supply-side and commodity price risks
- Management expects to ramp up production to meet demand and build on the strong H2 momentum into FY27
- GST 2.0 rollout in September 2025 simplified tax slabs and reduced GST on small cars/compact SUVs to 18% (removing cess), driving a sharp H2 demand revival and momentum heading into FY27
- Industry growth has been disproportionately strong in Sub Compact, Compact and Mid SUVs, reinforcing India's structural preference for SUV bodystyles, alongside strong growth in CNG and EV powertrains
- EV adoption accelerated on continued 5% GST for EVs, strong OEM participation, new high-aspiration launches, and charging infrastructure surpassing 30,000 public charging stations
- Rising customer expectations for in-vehicle technology (ADAS, auto park assist) and safety (5-star ratings) are setting new benchmarks across segments
- JLR performance was impacted by incremental US tariffs on UK/EU exports to the USA and a Q2 cyber incident that paused production for five weeks
- JLR retail sales were affected by the pause in US sales amid tariff uncertainty, the planned wind-down of legacy Jaguar models ahead of the new Jaguar launch, and China's luxury tax capturing a larger share of the model range
- Tata Sierra launch generated strong customer response with over 70,000 bookings on Day 1, reflecting brand strength in the premium mid-SUV space

Pursuant to the Composite Scheme of Arrangement demerging the Commercial Vehicle business, the Chinchwad facility in Pune, Maharashtra became part of the Company (TMPVL) with effect from October 2025, adding a manufacturing site to the PV business. The Company also expanded its dealer network, adding more than 100 sales outlets and more than 100 service outlets during the year. R&D and capex investments toward product sustainability -- particularly zero-emission products and battery electric vehicle technologies -- are undertaken through TPEML (Tata Passenger Electric Mobility Limited), the Company's wholly owned subsidiary.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic on demand; Aggressive on cost mitigation; Transparent on JLR challenges; Disciplined on inventory management; Focused on execution of launches.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Market leader in Indian EVs for 7 consecutive years with 40.2% market share and cumulative EV sales past 250,000 units
- Second-largest OEM in the Indian domestic PV market in H2 FY26 with 14.2% market share, growing at nearly twice the industry rate
- Balanced multi-powertrain strategy (ICE, CNG, EV) driving broad-based growth across SUVs, hatchbacks and CNG variants
- JLR's House of Brands structure -- four distinctive British brands (Range Rover, Defender, Discovery, Jaguar), each with shared design/engineering/technology foundations
- Doubled its sales and service network across India over the past few years, enhancing customer access and convenience

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Middle East conflict impacting supply chain (freight, petrochemicals) and MENA demand (6% mix); Geopolitical tariffs (US); Commodity inflation (Aluminum/Copper); JLR warranty costs; Regulatory volatility (CAFE, Made in Europe).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: JLR's breakeven volume reset to 300k units is critical to offset structural tariff/FX costs; PV's EV profitability trajectory is deflationary vs inflationary ICE due to emission norms; Freelander resurrection generates royalty/toll revenue without capex burden on JLR.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Multi-powertrain strategy spanning ICE, CNG and EV to cater to diverse mobility needs and comprehensively cover customer segments and price points
- Continued portfolio strengthening through new nameplates (e.g. Sierra) and mid-cycle refreshes (Altroz, Punch, Harrier, Safari) across hatchbacks, sedans and SUVs
- Network expansion and digital/AI-enabled customer experience improvements across sales, service and the ownership journey
- Cost optimisation through value engineering and commercial levers to mitigate commodity headwinds; de-bottlenecking production capacity across plants
- Addressing EV …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Commodity inflation (5-6%) and supply chain disruptions from Middle East conflict squeezing margins despite volume growth. | Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd | loser | Med | Volume leverage offset by inability to fully pass on costs immediately; margin recovery dependent on successful price hikes and cost-out programs in FY27. |
| Cyber incident aftermath, tariffs, and FX headwinds depressing full-year profits, requiring aggressive GBP 1.7bn cost reduction to restore profitability. | Jaguar Land Rover (within Tata Motors) | loser | High | Structural cost base misaligned with current volume/tariff environment; success hinges on flawless execution of new launches and procurement restructuring. |
| Intensifying competition in EV segment and potential demand softness due to fuel price volatility. | Competitor OEMs (Generic) | loser | Low | Tata's established EV ecosystem and CNG dominance create a moat, forcing competitors to fight on price in a cost-inflationary environment. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Name change] The filing is made by Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited, 'formerly Tata Motors Limited' / 'formerly known as Tata Motors Limited'; results are for the first quarter ended June 30, 2026.
- [Partnership] Signing of an MoU with Stellantis to collaborate on product development in the US, listed among Q1 FY27 key highlights.
- [Regulation - domestic demand] PV industry volumes of 1.3mn units were 'supported by robust post-GST 2.0 demand environment', with industry growth of 24% YoY on high growth in green powertrains (EV & CNG) and a low base effect.
- [Post-quarter financing] Changes to debt and liquidity since 30 June 2026: a further £500m was drawn from the £2bn syndicated loan facility on 23 July 2026 with the final £500m drawn on 13 August 2026, the proceeds of the final drawdown to be used for early repayment of the €298m bond maturing in November 2026.
- [Outlook risk] 'Implications from global geopolitical developments and luxury segment industry trends continue to be key monitorable', with financial performance 'to remain prudent as we deliver on our mid to long-term strategy'.
